doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bravo Brubeck and playing in Mexico
summary: He recorded Bravo Brubeck with Mexican musicians the year before and played cheap park concerts.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You had just gone there the year before, and that’s where you did the Bravo Brubeck. You used Mexican musicians.
He says because Bravo Brubeck had come out.
Yes. He’d been there before. I think the spillover from California, too, that the relationship with Mexico – there’s always been a big following.
That’s right. A lot of people come across that border into California for a year, go back.

We were playing in the big park. When you go to Mexico, you play in Bayes Artes, downtown, and it costs a lot. The next day, you’re in the park. It’s usually a Sunday afternoon, and it’s almost free. I think we added it up that it was 52 cents for a ticket. Maybe six to ten thousand people. We played there. How did I get the Mexican musicians?
Year before. We just played tunes I’d known from California. No rehearsal. I tried to have a rehearsal, but the Mexicans never came on the right day.
That tour, that recording, is probably Paul’s greatest solo, which is [inaudible].
That’s a beautiful recording. Let’s take a break here. We’re making good progress. We’re down to . . .
